source_title: UN commission says Israel has continued to commit genocide in Gaza since truce
source_excerpt:
Israel dismisses report as 'misinformation'
A United Nations commission says Israel ​continued to commit genocide in Gaza after last October's U.S.-brokered ceasefire in the enclave, in a report published Monday that Israel dismissed as part of a "misinformation campaign."
The report by the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian ‌Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel examined violations against Palestinian children since the start of the war between Israel and Hamas on Oct. 7, 2023, up to September this year.
It said Israeli authorities had kept committing "genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, ​in whole or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza."
The commission also accused Israeli soldiers and prison guards of war crimes and crimes against humanity in the West Bank, including extermination, torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence and persecution against civilians.
The commission said that it had recently documented six cases in which Israeli guards were sexually violent toward male detainees from Gaza in the Sde Teiman military prison.
Another report by the commission in September last year found that Israel had committed genocide in ​Gaza and that top Israeli officials including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu incited these acts — ⁠accusations that Israel called ⁠scandalous.
The Israeli mission in Geneva said the ‌latest report was part of a misinformation campaign to demonize Israel.
“The attempt to destroy the Jewish state ... continues today through efforts by actors such as the UN Commission of Inquiry to undermine Israel’s legitimacy and deny its fundamental right to exist and defend ⁠itself," Ambassador Daniel Meron said in a statement.
Life is brutal inside Gaza, one year into the ceasefire
The commission found that Israeli forces continued using heavy munitions, drones, quadcopters, artillery and sniper fire in densely populated areas during the ceasefire ‌in Gaza.
It said the "Yellow Line" which was presented as a temporary ceasefire demarcation, was encroaching increasingly into Gaza, and becoming a de facto border, which the report said reflected Israel’s expanding territorial control of Gaza.
Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Israel's ​assault on Gaza, launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people, according to Israeli goverment tallies, in southern Israel on Oct. 7, 2023.

In its report to the ⁠UN Security Council, the commission said the situation in the West Bank had also deteriorated sharply, with the ⁠number of Palestinians killed in airstrikes increasing from six between 2008 and Oct. 6, 2023, to ⁠254 between ⁠Oct. 7, 2023, and Sept. 30, ​2026.
Commission Chair Srinivasan Muralidhar said the intentional killing of Palestinian civilians and destruction of homes in the West ​Bank formed part of a ⁠broader strategy to exterminate and displace Palestinians.
Military operations since January 2025 have led to the largest displacement of Palestinians in the West Bank since 1967, with 34,176 Palestinians remaining displaced as of August 2026, the report said.
The commission also faulted the Palestinian Authority, saying it had targeted Palestinians who voice dissenting views and that journalists and ⁠human rights defenders had been ‌killed and injured.
